label: input a at t=2 completing a sequence-initial "2 u a" / "c u a" trigram
explanation: A very sparse trigram detector. It fires only in the original phase, on the input token a when the sequence opens with "2 u a" or "c u a" (a at t=2). The prefix sets the magnitude: "2 u a" gives the max activation (~0.49), and "c u a" gives only ~0.025 (about 5% of max), so roughly 93% of activation mass comes from the "2 u" opening. The few other firings are "3 2 u a" at t=3, which are also weak (~0.027). It does not fire on the same "2 u a" or "c u a" trigram when it appears later in the sequence (t>=3, apart from the 3-2-u-a case), on any other token after "u", or in the delimiter or copy phases (including when "2 u a" is re-fed during copying). The predicate misses only the two weak 3-2-u-a firings on dev.

issues: The core claims hold. On the dev split all 26 firings are in the original phase: 24 at t=2 (99% of mass) and 2 at t=3. There are zero firings in the delimiter or copy phases, and every firing has in_tok = a.

The magnitude split checks out. On the t=2 '2 u a' opening, the 2-prefix carries 92.3% of dev mass (91.5% on test) and the c-prefix carries 6.6% (6.2% on test). Both sub-predicates have precision 1.0 on both splits: 10/10 and 16/16 for '2 u a', 14/14 and 21/21 for 'c u a'.

One claim in the explanation is wrong. It says the t=3 '_ 2 u a' firings are 'also weak (~0.027)' and occur only for the '3 2 u a' case. The single test miss is 'o 2 u [a:0.40]' at t=3, at 40% of max, so it is not weak and the prefix is not 3. That one step holds 2.3% of test mass.

The t=3 firings are a rare, prefix-dependent tail, not a general rule. On dev, the '2 u a' trigram at t=3 occurs 18 times but fires only twice (precision 0.11), both with orig(0)=3. On test it occurs 19 times and fires once, with orig(0)=o. The explanation should say that '2 u a' at t=3 almost never fires, with occasional firings (for example after 3 or o) that can be strong.

Extending the predicate with a t=3 clause for orig(0) in {3, o} gives dev F1 1.0 and test F1 0.974. That is not better than the original test F1 of 0.987, and the clause is ad hoc. The remaining gap is a 1-step tail, not a systematic counterexample class, so the label and predicate stand.
